b: A cot. The blanket is embroidered: WALKED IT OFF.
L: A crate of bandages, unopened. Doctor Mog doesn't believe in them.
1: The way out, to the drill yard.

objects.name: Doctor Mog
lines: Broken arm? Walk it off. Bad cough? Walk it off. Head on backwards? Walk it off.
Forty years. Not one patient's come back to complain. I think they walked it off.

answer: Course it does. Look at my waiting room. Everybody's walking.
…Round in a circle. Mostly. Some of them have been walking since spring.

questions.ask: You're not a doctor, you're a shrug.
answer: A shrug that's never lost a patient.
Rudeness, is it? Nasty case. Walk it off.

objects.name: A patient
lines: Broke my leg. Doctor said walk it off.
I'm walking it off. Very slowly. This is day ninety.

questions.ask: Where do the dead go in here?
answer: Back room. Doctor Mog doesn't go in. Says that's the king's business.
Somebody stitches them. Then they walk out. Walking it off, I suppose. Better than me.
* He takes one step. It's very slow. He looks at you, proud.

objects.name: Another patient
lines: Arrow in the shoulder. Walk it off, he said.
I've walked to the bazaar and back eleven times. Still there. Very fit now, though.

answer: The back door opens at night. Feet go out. Not living feet. Stitchy feet.
Don't ask Mog. Mog says walk it off. Walk what off? He won't say.

questions.ask: Just pull the arrow out yourself.
answer: Pull it out? Then what've I got? A hole.
Arrow's part of me now. I hang my hat on it.
